title: Using Claude Opus 5.5 as your daily driver
format_note: Presenter-led model-launch walkthrough: talking head cut against real desktop-app screen recordings, side-by-side comparison, then settings tips.
one_thing: Opus 5.5 on medium effort is faster and cheaper than Opus 5, and here is when to switch to high.

transcript.voice_style: Conversational first-person presenter; casual fillers ('Okay so', 'Cool'); hedged honesty ('this is just my run').
transcript.script_shape: Claims first (faster, cheaper, +25% limits), then a live A/B proof, then a counter-case where high effort wins, two config tips, one command, short sign-off.

structure.frame0: Presenter mid-smile in a warm dark home-office set; no title in the first frame, wordmark 'Claude Opus 5.5' appears by 1.17 s (strips/window-01-0s.jpg).
structure.first_3s: Presenter speaks straight to camera; title top-left at 1.2 s, subline 'Compared to Opus 5' and first claim 'Faster' follow by 3.5 s while she says the release line.

beats.what: Presenter states four gains while a five-line stat list builds beside her.
'Let's run them side by side'; cream stage, app windows slide in, same prompt typed in both.
Opus 5 and 5.5 windows side by side; 5.5 finishes with a short answer while Opus 5 keeps reading.
Usage popover shows 5-hour limit 4% for 5.5 versus 6% for Opus 5.
Effort defaults to medium; effort slider and tooltip explained.
Rename task on medium: handler edited, tests pass, mobile serializer file missed.
Same task on High traces the mobile client, edits serializer and schema, adds a test.
Subagent tip: model: sonnet in explore.md and CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL in settings.json.
Presenter recaps: medium by default, high for multi-file changes, Sonnet or Haiku for read-only subagents.
/claude-api prompt-audit typed and run; reads CLAUDE.md and SKILL.md, edits both.
Presenter sums up and asks viewers to try 5.5 and send feedback.
Cream card: coral star appears, then 'Claude Code' wordmark.

hero_moment.what: 5.5's whole answer sits on screen (cause, tests, one snag, one question) while Opus 5 is still listing file reads (sheet-02, 44 s).

ending.cta_text: Spoken only: 'go try out Opus 5.5 and let me know what you think.' No on-screen CTA.
ending.what: Cream card with coral star then 'Claude Code' wordmark, centred, held to the end (f0104.jpg, f0106.jpg).

on_screen_lines.text: Faster than Opus 5 on the same task
Better answers shorter, clearer about what to do next
20% cheaper per token $4 in, $20 out per million tokens
25% more usage on Pro, Max and Team limits
~40% cheaper per task it needs fewer tokens to get to a result
Fix #418: refunds on orders that used discount codes come out a few cents off, and refunding an order item by item doesn't add up...

good.observation: The comparison is shown rather than claimed: identical prompt typed in two windows, so the viewer sees 5.5 finish while Opus 5 is still reading.
Real product UI with a real cursor, real file names and real numbers (4% versus 6%, 41 of 41 passing) makes each claim checkable.
A counter-case (medium misses the mobile serializer) is shown before the advice, so 'use high here' is earned.
Stat list builds line by line beside the speaker and persists, giving five must-carry facts at 4.0-6.9% heading height.
Scale-up crops put small UI controls (effort slider, usage popover) at readable size instead of showing the full window.
Restrained palette: coral only for the star and code, green/red only for diff counts, so attention goes to the content.

weak.observation: Full-window split-screen frames carry 11-13 px UI text that is unreadable at phone width; the comparison relies on voice.
The 25% overlay line appears about 2.4 s after the spoken '25% further' at 8 s, so text trails speech.
No on-screen call to action; the ask to try 5.5 is spoken only and the end card carries only the product wordmark.
20 hard cuts and talking-head stretches of 8-20 s repeat one framing, so the film leans on the voice for variety.

rule_candidates.rule: In presenter-led explainers, build must-carry numbers as a persistent list that adds one line per spoken claim, headings 4-7% of frame height with 2.9% captions beneath.
rule_candidates.evidence: f0004.jpg, f0007.jpg; list of five lines held 1.2-17.9 s; 29-50 px headings of 720

rule_candidates.rule: Prove a comparative claim with a split screen running identical input; put the cut to the result at the moment the faster side finishes.
rule_candidates.evidence: Split screen 34.6-66.8 s; 5.5 summary on screen at 44 s versus Opus 5 reading

rule_candidates.rule: For screen-recording tutorials, long shots of 8-32 s are acceptable when on-screen activity changes every 1-2 s; the 1.8-3.5 s cut rule applies to launch films.
Zoom small interface controls to fill 40% or more of the frame width before asking the viewer to read them; do not show the full window.
rule_candidates.evidence: f0045.jpg zoom shows 24 px popover text; f0032.jpg split window shows 11-13 px text

rule_candidates.rule: A speech-driven film may be almost all hard cuts when each cut lands on a topic change in the voice; no dissolves needed.
rule_candidates.evidence: 20 hard cuts; first at 22.87 on 'let's run them side by side'

rule_candidates.rule: Open on the subject with the title arriving within 1.5 s; add a 'sped up' pill whenever recorded time is compressed.
rule_candidates.evidence: strips/window-01-0s.jpg title at 1.17 s; f0019.jpg 'sped up' pill

rule_candidates.rule: End on a clean brand card held at least 5 s, with the mark animating in before the wordmark; put any call to action in on-screen text too.
rule_candidates.evidence: 205.4-212.5 s card, 7.1 s; f0104.jpg star then f0106.jpg wordmark

rule_candidates.rule: Voice-only social uploads can sit at -16 LUFS integrated with -3.5 dBTP peak and 2.6 LU range; speech clarity, not loudness, is the gate.
